title: Operator handbook: mini-workshop observability canvas
body:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact, hands-on canvas for operator onboarding sessions (30–60m).
Target audience: oncall engineers, SREs, new observability contributors, and solutions engineers who need a quick reference to the minimal signal set, tracing conventions, and dashboard widget recipes for inference services.

How to use this doc (workshop flow):
1) 5m — Context and goals: what failure modes we prioritize (latency regressions, cold-cache tenant impacts, fallbacks, token-surge cost spikes).
2) 10m — Signal mapping exercise: pick a route/model and map user-visible symptom -> service-level metric -> trace anchor -> dashboard widget.
3) 15m — Instrumentation checklist: ensure event, metric, and span coverage for that route.
4) 10m — Build a compact dashboard using the widget recipes below and agree on 1–2 alert thresholds.
5) 5–20m — Retro: gaps, next steps, owner assignment.

Minimal signal set (operators' quick reference):
- Request-per-second (rps): per-route, per-tenant (rolling 1m, 5m).
- P50/P90/P99 end-to-end latency (ms): measured at API gateway and at model runtime.
- Token throughput: tokens/s and tokens/request (mean, p95).
- KV cache hit-rate: prefix cache hits / prefix cache lookups (per-model variant).
- Queue/backlog length: pending requests in batcher and router queue (absolute + per-GPU).
- Error rate: 4xx and 5xx separated; include classification for fallback-triggered errors.
- Model-fallback events: count and ratio of requests routed to fallback variant.
- Cost-proxy: estimated tokens * model-cost-factor per-minute (approx for quick triage).
- Synthetic-probe success and latency: per-region and per-availability zone.

Definitions and instrumentation notes (short):
- "End-to-end latency": time from first byte of client request to last byte of streaming response chunk or final response close. Tag with route_id, model_id, tenant_id, trace_id.
- "Runtime latency": time inside the serving runtime from model forward-start to forward-end. Tag with model_variant, device_type, batch_size.
- "KV cache hit-rate": emit counters for kv_cache.hit and kv_cache.miss with same tags; compute hit-rate in dashboards and guards.
- "Token throughput": emit counter tokens.emitted incremented per output token; also counter tokens.consumed per request.
- "Fallback event": emit an event log when routing policy sends request to fallback; include reason tag (capacity|latency|error).

Tracing conventions (concise):
- Root span: api.request (name should be route:<route_id> or route:chat.create). Root carries tenant_id and request_id.
- Child spans and timing anchors:
  - gateway.auth (fast auth checks)
  - router.lookup (route resolution + policy decision)
  - batcher.enqueue and batcher.dequeue (include queue_time ms)
  - runtime.forward (model forward pass) with tags: model_variant, seq_len, batch_size, device, quantization
  - runtime.kv_cache.lookup (emit sampled spans for long KV ops)
  - network.call.<external> for calls to third-party tools
- Span baggage: avoid large payloads, but include a compact eval_seed or prompt_hash to link to prompt-replay storage for high-severity incidents.
- Sampling policy: preserve 100% sampling for synthetic-probe traces and sampled 5–10% for high-traffic routes (adaptive sampling for p99-exceed traces).

Dashboard layout recipes (compact five-panel board):
Panel 1 — What users feel: end-to-end latency heatmap
  - Data: p50/p90/p99 by route and tenant cohort over 1h window, heatmap by time-of-day and region.
  - Intent: surface regressions and tenant-specific spikes.
Panel 2 — Serving bottlenecks: runtime latency + queue backlog
  - Data: runtime.forward p50/p95, batcher queue length, device GPU utilization.
  - Intent: decide whether to scale or reduce batching.
Panel 3 — Efficiency guardrails: KV cache hit-rate and token economics
  - Data: kv_cache.hit_rate (last 5m), tokens/request, approximate cost-proxy rate.
  - Intent: detect cache churn or token regressions that increase cost.
Panel 4 — Reliability signals: error rates and fallback ratio
  - Data: 5xx rate, fallback_event ratio, synthetic-probe failures.
  - Intent: triage whether failure is model-related, infra, or routing policy.
Panel 5 — Investigation aids: top traces and prompt-replay quick links
  - Data: list of top 10 traces with longest runtime.forward or highest queue_time; include link to prompt-replay object and relevant GitHub/Jira references.

Widget recipes (copy-paste friendly text):
- Latency heatmap: group by route_id, quantize by minute, display p95 and p99 bands; color thresholds: green <200ms, amber 200–500ms, red >500ms.
- Queue gauge: max backlog across batchers; alert if > 200 requests for > 2m for high-tier customers.
- KV hit-rate sparkline: compute 5m rolling average; alert if drops > 15 percentage points vs 1h baseline.
- Fallback ratio bar: stacked by reason tag (capacity|latency|error); alert when ratio > 3% sustained 10m.
- Token-cost rate: moving sum tokens * cost_factor per minute; useful for capacity planning spikes.

Suggested alert thresholds (operator defaults — adjust per-customer):
- p99 end-to-end latency > 1s sustained 5m -> Pager (severity 1) for Dedicated customers.
- runtime.forward p95 > 700ms for model_variant=large -> Pager (severity 2).
- kv_cache.hit_rate drop > 20 percentage points compared to 1h median for same route -> Page oncall (severity 2).
- fallback ratio > 5% for > 10m -> Ops email + runbook review (severity 3).
- synthetic-probe failures in any region > 2 of last 3 probes -> Alert channel notification (severity 2).

Investigation runbook (quick):
1) Confirm whether user-visible latency or token cost spike. Check Panel 1 and 3.
2) Open a trace from Panel 5; look for long batcher.enqueue->dequeue gaps or runtime.forward high duration.
3) If queue backlog high, examine autoscale metrics and GPU utilization. Scale or route to fallback variant as temporary mitigation.
4) If kv_cache hit-rate low, check recent routing or model changes and cache invalidation pushes.
5) If fallback ratio high with reason=capacity, check scheduler logs and capacity reservations.
6) If error classification points to model (bad outputs), pull model version and recent rollout history (use rollout dashboard link).

Instrumentation checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Emit root span api.request with tenant_id, route_id, request_id, and prompt_hash.
- [ ] Emit runtime.forward spans with batch_size and seq_len tags.
- [ ] Counters: requests.count, tokens.emitted, tokens.consumed.
- [ ] Cache counters: kv_cache.hit, kv_cache.miss.
- [ ] Queue metrics: queue.length (per-batcher) and queue.time histogram.
- [ ] Emit fallback.event logs with reason and target_variant.
- [ ] Synthetic probes deployed for each region/zone with success+latency metrics.
- [ ] Link traces to stored prompt-replay objects (ID only).

Open questions and backlog items:
- How do we normalize cost-proxy across model variants with transient discounts? (ACTION: product + finance to provide cost_factors; owner: Marco)
- Should we surface tenant-level p99 SLA windows in the same dashboard or separate per-customer pages? (ACTION: SRE + Solutions to prototype two variants)
- Define standard adaptive sampling rates per traffic tier and retention policy for traces. (ACTION: Observability infra)

Quick wins for next iteration:
- Add a compact widget template library in Grafana/Looker for the five-panel board so teams can import.
- Automate prompt_hash redaction and storage link generation at ingestion.
- Create a small training deck (10 slides) based on this canvas for new hires.

References and links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-OBS-42 (observability standards)
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-211 (dashboard import library epic)
- GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-widgets (widget recipes repo)

Notes to self / workshop reminders:
- Keep the session interactive: ask participating operators to sketch their route and write down two likely failure modes.
- Emphasize correlation-first debugging: metric -> trace -> replay.
- Capture one action and one owner at the end of each session.

Revision log:
- 2024-02-15: initial draft (Lena)
- 2024-03-02: added widget recipes and alert thresholds (Marco)
- 2024-04-10: clarified tracing sampling guidance and added checklist (Aisha)
